chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who has a concubine, and his son mounts her and has intercourse with her. He said: There was a man who had a concubine and a wife, and he ordered his son to mount his father's concubine, and the son had intercourse with her. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about that, and he said: It does not prohibit the father from having intercourse with her, but it is not fitting for him to approach her until she is cleared of the son's offspring. If offspring results from what is between them, the offspring belongs to the father, provided they both had intercourse with her in one day and one month.

key_terms.الْوَلَدُ لِلْأَبِ: The offspring belongs to the father

ai.seo_question: Does a son's intercourse with his father's concubine prohibit the father from having intercourse with her?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) regarding the paternity of a concubine impregnated by her master's son, establishing that the father retains his right to intercourse but is advised to wait for the son's offspring to be cleared (*istibra*). The hadith clarifies that if the father also impregnates her within the same day and month, the child is attributed to him, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of *istibra* in determining lineage. This narration highlights the practical application of paternity laws in the context of concubinage (*milk al-yamin*) prevalent in early Islamic society.
